_README: The current Northern Colorado market report, shown on /northern-colorado-market-report.html.
THIS IS THE ONLY FILE TO EDIT EACH MONTH. Change the figures, change `month`, run
`python3 build/build.py`, commit and push. The page, its schema, and the 'as of' line
IF YOU MISS A MONTH the build prints a loud warning once the report is more than 45
days old, and the page itself says how old it is rather than pretending to be current.
That is deliberate: a hub page silently claiming June figures in November is worse
than no page at all, because it advertises neglect on the one page that exists to
prove you are on top of the market.
Every figure comes from IRES MLS. Aggregate statistics only -- medians, days on
market, sale-to-list ratios, counts. Individual listing content (addresses, photos,
specific list prices) is what the IDX terms restrict, which is why addresses are held
privately here, the same rule sold_homes.json follows.
Set a field to null and it is simply left off the page rather than rendered empty.

region.weighted_median_note: Weighted by each town's sale count, so a handful of sales in a small town cannot skew the regional figure.

takeaway: Sellers are still landing close to ask, and buyers are winning on the homes that were priced properly to begin with. In the $1M+ tier days on market run longer because those buyers are deliberate rather than hesitant -- pricing precision, not pricing volume, decides whether a luxury property trades inside 60 days or sits for six months.
